1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 d6 4.d4 Bd7 5.Nc.strategy: Brings the king to safety and keeps all the pressure on e5 and the option of exchanging on c6. It is the sound way to continue development; Black must soon decide how to resolve the tension in the centre.

Trades the bishop for the knight to remove a defender of e5, but Black recaptures with the bishop, so the pawn structure stays intact and e5 is not really attacked. White gives up the bishop pair for little in return.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 d6 4.d4 Bd7 5.Nc.name: Ruy Lopez: Steinitz Defence, Nimzowitsch Attack

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 d6 4.d4 Bd7 5.Nc.strategy: Develops the bishop and prepares to castle, but only once the centre is settled: with White's rook heading for e1, castling at once runs into a tactic that loses material, so Black will have to exchange on d4. Solid, but passive.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 d6 4.d4 Bd7 5.Nc.name: Ruy Lopez: Berlin Defence, Hedgehog Variation

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 d6 4.d4 Bd7 5.Nc.strategy: Resolves the centre at once, before White's rook reaches the e-file, and so avoids the tactics around castling. The price is the e5 stronghold: White's knight recaptures into the centre with a freer game, but Black's pieces are well placed and the structure is sound.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 d6 4.d4 Bd7 5.Nc.name: Ruy Lopez: Berlin Defence, Closed Wolf Variation
